Chapter library

Compact simulation review: the complete written library

47 written chapters, 1,040 distinct stored or default-computed models and 7,124 exact checkpoints were reviewed individually. The interface also covers repeated appearances of models inside worked solutions.

Size and reading

Every simulation stays inside its lesson column. Figures use a maximum normal width of 760 pixels. Zoom enlarges only the drawing inside a bounded, scrollable frame. Mobile figures can be panned inside that frame; the page itself does not expand.

Follow a computation

  1. Start with the paused, exact checkpoint. Read the operation, its reason, formula and recorded quantities.
  2. Use Next or Previous for one operation. Before and Compare show exact stored states; no arithmetic values are interpolated.
  3. Pause freezes the current movement. Play resumes it. The Transition slider lets you inspect geometric progress.
  4. Copy and dependency markers follow the existing connected route. They illustrate the operation order, rather than asserting physical circuit delay or intermediate numerical states.
  5. Read Exact changes, the invariant and Full exact state. Dense probability distributions have a separate exact mass table.
  6. Browse all operations to locate a specific step. Keyboard navigation and reduced-motion mode remain available.

Individual scientific diagrams

Circuit gates and nets, Karnaugh maps, matrix entries, geometric constructions, probability axes, data structures and recursive calls keep their own scientific representations. Consistency concerns the reading interface and interaction controls. Valid domain geometry is retained, while deficient label placement, replay or explanation is corrected. Mathematical derivations keep native MathML instead of receiving an unrelated diagram.

Checks and limits

All used checkpoints passed browser rendering, glyph bounds, padding, label collision and available endpoint checks. Every written chapter passed stored-model coverage, contained width, mobile overflow, enlarged-text and standard-control checks. Live replay was checked in eight representative chapters, including pause/resume, transition scrubbing, zoom, adjustable-model replacement, printing and reduced motion. Lessons, worked questions, final rules and stored scientific model files match the frozen baseline. This is a finite software and visual audit; it does not claim a mathematical guarantee for every future input or every examination question.
